Mike Stearman was our first man home in 6th place, then came Brian Trower 12th, Don McLean 14th, and Brian Rice 21st. Both Trower and MacLean are in the Forces, while Rice is at Cambridge University, and J.

Brian Trower was 37th, with Mike Stearman 40th, and Mike was another just getting over the 'flu, and then came Don McLean, 65. We were pleased to see Geoff Goode out once again, and he looked short of training and has also put on quite a bit of weight in the Army.

The mile which followed was won by Ingles of T.V.H. but Ray Tooby and Don McLean, both putting in a rare appearance, finished 2nd and 3rd. The quarter gave another opportunity for young Stephens to add to our score and this he ably did by securing 3rd place.
Don McLean came all the way from Oxford by motor-cycle to finish 324th - perhaps the cold got into his bones, or is there some other reason for these continuous lapses from his real form?

In fact their last minute timing (not for the first time!) prompted the question as to whether Don McLean's 'title' was in jeopardy!!.It was good to see steeple-chasers John Bicourt and Dick Piotrowski out on the road, at what is a slightly longer than usual distance for them,as well as being a tough race.
